title: Value In Finite Zero-Sum Perfect-Information Games
body_html:
Value In Finite Zero-Sum Perfect-Information Games

Every finite zero-sum perfect-information game, with or without Nature, has a value and both players have pure optimal strategies.
proof_html:
Sketch

Use forward induction on the tree. If Nature moves at the root, the value is the probability-weighted average of the successor subgame values. If player 1 moves, the value is the maximum of successor values; if player 2 moves, it is the minimum. Optimal pure strategies are obtained by choosing an optimal successor and then following optimal strategies in the selected subgame.

References

  • [MFoGT, Prop. 6.2.5] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Every finite zero-sum perfect-information game with or without Nature has a value and pure optimal strategies.
